history.rationale: Initial seed policy baseline on stratified val (12 tasks).

Root causes are (1) a non-static partition predicate `ds = (SELECT MAX(ds) ...)` was rejected by ODPS partition pruning, so the query needed `MAX_PT('<table>')` or a literal partition value; and (2) a successfully returning query with non-empty rows was silently wrong because a business-date range was constrained by the partition key instead of the business-date column, dropping late-arriving/zero-amount rows. The refiner only acted on gateway errors and lacked a mandatory Post-Execution Sanity & Caliber Audit for non-empty results.

Primary root cause is upstream schema linking that was too permissive and under-probed. In the first trajectory, WarehouseLinker finalized without probing opaque status/type code columns and an ambiguous BIGINT amount column; its schema_notes carried unverified human-readable status literals and a guessed cent-to-yuan conversion. The generator used those guesses, and the refiner only repaired partition pruning but accepted a non-empty result with zero conditional aggregates. In the second trajectory, the linker probed but over-translated a compound business condition into an extra operational-status predicate, silently dropping rows. Downstream modules cannot recover from unverified code/unit metadata and over-specified filters.

Silent caliber misses originate in DialectSQLGenerator: it treated the daily partition key as a full business-date range filter, so backfilled/out-of-range row-by-row business dates could survive partition pruning. The current generator prompt is too sparse to consistently enforce ODPS date-format alignment, dual partition/business-date filters, grain pre-aggregation, SCD2 interval joins, probed code/unit semantics, and explicit window frames; the refiner repaired one symptom, but the generator should emit first-pass-correct SQL.

Sampled trajectories passed the gateway and matched gold rows exactly, so there is no active dialect/partition error. The main latent risk is generator-side under-specification for three recurring warehouse patterns: partition-window vs business-date filter asymmetry, SCD2 point-in-time attribution with pre-aggregated multi-row facts, and dimension-preserving zero-fill LEFT JOIN analytics with per-row net/floor semantics. Strengthening these guards in DialectSQLGenerator reduces future silent caliber defects without restricting already-valid behavior.

Stage-1 val screen not cleared (EX=80.0%): The gateway passed and the query returned non-empty rows, so GatewayRefiner skipped the mandatory Post-Execution Sanity & Caliber Audit and returned the same SQL. The SQL has silent caliber defects: a nullable test/flag predicate with `= 0` drops rows where the flag is NULL; a multi-row fact/detail table was deduplicated by `ROW_NUMBER()` instead of pre-aggregating additive amounts to the join grain, causing understated sums; and the current-latest SCD2 categorical tier was computed with `MAX(tier)` rather than selecting the deterministic latest current row, silently excluding changed-category orders. These are exactly the non-empty result-mismatch cases GatewayRefiner must catch.
